title: The Canvas & UI System Overview
description: Understand the Canvas, render modes, and how Unity separates UI from the game world.

slides.title: What is a Canvas? 🖼️
slides.content:
# The Drawing Board

In Unity, all UI elements (text, buttons, images) must live inside a **Canvas**. The Canvas is a special GameObject that renders UI on top of (or as part of) the scene.

- Without a Canvas, you cannot see UI elements.
- When you create any UI element (GameObject → UI → Text), Unity automatically creates a Canvas if one doesn't exist.
- The Canvas uses its own coordinate system, not world units.

quizData.question: What must all UI elements be placed inside?
quizData.explanation: A Canvas is the root for all UI rendering.

slides.title: Render Modes 🎥
slides.content:
# How the Canvas Appears

The Canvas component has three **Render Modes**:

- **Screen Space – Overlay**: UI is rendered on top of everything. Always visible, no camera needed. Perfect for HUDs and menus.
- **Screen Space – Camera**: UI is rendered in screen space but positioned by a specific camera. Good for effects, depth.
- **World Space**: The Canvas is a 3D object in the scene. UI is placed in the world (e.g., floating nameplates, in‑game monitors).

You switch modes in the Canvas component.

quizData.question: Which render mode is best for a health bar floating above a player's head?
quizData.explanation: World Space places UI in the 3D environment, following the player.

slides.title: The Canvas Scaler ⚖️
slides.content:
# Handling Different Screen Sizes

Attached to the Canvas is the **Canvas Scaler**. It controls how UI scales to fit different screen resolutions.

- **Constant Pixel Size**: UI stays exactly the same pixel size (bad for different screens).
- **Scale With Screen Size**: UI scales relative to a reference resolution (e.g., 1920x1080). This is the most common setting.
- **Constant Physical Size**: uses DPI.

For adaptive UI, set UI Scale Mode to **Scale With Screen Size**, Reference Resolution to 1920x1080, and Match to 0.5 (width/height blend).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Multiple Canvases

For complex UIs, use multiple Canvases: one for the background, one for pop‑ups. But remember, more Canvases means more draw calls. Use them sparingly.
